- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.10) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward → reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.  
- If model forecasts a sharp spike (e.g. +10%+ above recent mean) and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, it often overestimates → cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.  
- Model underestimates true mean reversion when sentiment is negative → adjust downward by 2–5% in 3–5 day horizon if recent price is above 30-day MA.  
- If forecast is >15% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply “lag correction”: subtract 1–3% per day from forecast for next 5 days.  
- When sentiment is positive (avg > 0.05) and model is flat or slightly rising, it often underestimates → add 2–5% to forecast for next 3–7 days.  
- If true outcome exceeds model by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, assume momentum → forecast next 3 days should be 1–3% above model.  
- Model tends to ignore sentiment when price is near 30-day MA → if sentiment is negative and price is near MA, forecast should be 1–3% below MA.
